title: Northern Grid - Private VPC discovery
summary: Intro discovery for Private/VPC deployment. Customer wants private endpoints in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, no public egress for inference traffic, BYOK KMS integration, SOC2/ISO questions, and a performance benchmark. Next step: SE deep dive + network diagram + security pack.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-18
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Northern Grid CTO), Samir Patel (Lead DevOps), Hannah Ng (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Ethan, our SE. Quick agenda, we want to understand your deployment constraints for Private / VPC, network topology, security requirements, and timelines.

[00:17] Lena: Thanks Maya. We run grid analytics and scheduling, sensitive PII in some messages, need everything inside our VPCs, no public internet egress for model payloads. We're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private but leaning Private because of data residency.

[00:32] Samir: Yeah we have two primary regions, us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Primary workloads in us-east-1. We use AWS Transit Gateway between accounts, multiple VPCs per account with overlapping services. Concern is CIDR overlap and peering restrictions.

[00:48] Ethan: Okay, makes sense. Redwood Private supports VPC deployment patterns a few ways: VPC peering, Transit Gateway attachments, or PrivateLink-style private endpoints. For your Transit Gateway setup we can attach a dedicated VPC owned by Redwood or we can accept a peering attachment - depends on your security posture.

[01:05] Hannah: Quick Q - we require BYOK (bring-your-own-key) with KMS/HSM. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS in the private deployment? Also audit logs must ship to our Splunk/S3 and we need 12 months retention.

[01:22] Maya: Yes, BYOK via KMS is supported in Private. We support customer-managed keys and can integrate with AWS KMS and on-prem HSM for some flows. Audit logs can be exported to your S3 or CloudWatch, and we also provide syslog/SFTP integration for SIEM. We'll include the specifics in the security pack.

[01:40] Samir: Good. On networking, do you require internet egress for model downloads or updates? We can't allow that out of our VPC.

[01:51] Ethan: For model lifecycle, if you opt for a fully private deployment we can seed models via an agreed secure channel - e.g., pre-baked AMIs or via an S3 bucket with VPC endpoint access and restricted IAM roles. In most private installs there is no outbound public egress required. There are a couple of operational calls back to the control plane if you use Redwood managed control plane; however, for strict air-gapped or fully private we offer an on-prem control plane variant or VPC-hosted control plane with private endpoints.

[02:18] Lena: What about region constraints - we need data residency in eu-west-1 for EU customers. Can we deploy a private instance in both regions and have routing between them?

[02:30] Maya: Yes, you can have region-specific Private deployments. We recommend local model serving in each region to meet latency and residency. Cross-region replication of logs and metrics is configurable; you can also keep logs in-region. We'll outline options in the follow-up doc.

[02:47] Samir: CIDR overlap is a real problem. Some of our older VPCs use 10.0.0.0/8 ranges that collide with third-party networks. How do you handle overlapping CIDRs for peering?

[03:00] Ethan: Overlapping CIDRs complicate direct peering. Options: 1) Transit Gateway with route table transformations if available, 2) use AWS PrivateLink / Private endpoints so we don't do full L3 peering - traffic goes to an endpoint IP inside your VPC, avoiding global CIDR conflicts, or 3) re-IP your app VPCs if possible. PrivateLink is often the least intrusive.

[03:20] Hannah: Do you support PrivateLink in both us-east-1 and eu-west-1? Are there limits on number of endpoints?

[03:28] Ethan: We can provision PrivateLink endpoints in both regions. There are AWS limits on endpoints per account but those are typically bumpable. We'll include recommended CIDRs and endpoint configs in the network requirements doc.

[03:40] Lena: From a security/compliance standpoint we need SAML SSO integration and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC, and audit trails tied to our IdP. Can Redwood integrate with Okta/Azure AD?

[03:54] Maya: Yes, we support SAML and SCIM. RBAC can be mapped to your SAML attributes and we support SCIM-based user provisioning. We'll include sample SAML metadata and claims as part of the security pack.

[04:10] Samir: Another consideration is latency - some of our control loops are 100-200ms sensitive. What are the latency implications of a private endpoint vs fully dedicated GPU pools?

[04:23] Ethan: If you colocate model serving in-region and access via private endpoint you'll get minimal added latency - typically single-digit ms on top of model inference. Dedicated GPU pools with reserved capacity improve tail latency by avoiding noisy neighbor effects; hosted shared pools might have slightly higher p50/p95 depending on load. We'll run a perf benchmark to quantify for your prompt mix.

[04:45] Hannah: Data retention: can you guarantee no token logs are retained outside our control? We need controls to disable logging or to route logs to our S3 only.

[04:56] Maya: In Private you can configure token-level logging and we can disable retention or route logs exclusively to your storage. We'll document the options: full off, PII redaction, or customer-only storage with retention TTL.

[05:10] Samir: Network firewall rules - what ports/IPs should we open? Any egress requirements to download container images or updates?

[05:20] Ethan: We'll provide a prescriptive ruleset. Typical rules: allow PrivateLink endpoint IPs, a small set of management IP ranges if you use Redwood-managed control plane (or zero if fully private), and route HTTPS to S3 endpoints for model artifact pulls if you choose that path. If you want zero public egress we can push images into your private ECR or provide preloaded images.

[05:41] Lena: Operational model - who manages upgrades and patches for the runtime? We need clear SLOs and maintenance windows.

[05:51] Maya: For Private deployments we have two models: you manage the runtime (self-managed) or Redwood manages it under a managed services add-on. Managed includes scheduled maintenance windows, patching, and a rollback playbook. Dedicated also has SLA-backed uptime. We'll include SLA language and recommended maintenance cadence.

[06:12] Speaker 1: (mumble) do we have a playbook for incident response?

[06:15] Ethan: Yes, incident response and runbooks are part of the enterprise bundle. We can integrate with your PagerDuty and provide tracing hooks.

[06:24] Hannah: For encryption in transit, mutual TLS or customer-side mTLS?

[06:29] Maya: Mutual TLS is supported; for PrivateLink traffic it's still over AWS internal network but we recommend mTLS and application-level encryption for defense-in-depth.

[06:38] Samir: Can we do network egress filtering from the Redwood side so only specific internal endpoints get traffic?

[06:45] Ethan: Yes, on the Redwood-hosted side we can configure egress allowlists for outbound calls. But in the fully private model, outbound is minimal. We'll show the configurations.

[06:56] Lena: Timeline - we want to start a pilot for a subset of endpoints in us-east-1 in the next 2-3 weeks. Is that feasible?

[07:05] Maya: Yes, feasible. Typical pilot path: 1) SE deep dive to finalize network diagram and access method (PrivateLink vs peering), 2) security review and SOC2 pack, 3) provisioning of private endpoint and small dedicated capacity for benchmark, 4) run sample workload. We can start step 1 this week.

[07:28] Samir: On the pilot we need to test throughput and token cost estimates. Can Redwood provide a cost model for dedicated GPU pools vs hosted?

[07:37] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Optimize will give batching/quantization recommendations and cost estimates per 1M tokens for each config. We'll provide a spreadsheet-based TCO for dedicated vs hosted vs private.

[07:50] Hannah: A couple of specific asks for the follow-up: SOC2 report, architecture diagram for PrivateLink and Transit Gateway patterns, sample SAML metadata, and a list of required CIDRs and ports.

[08:03] Maya: Noted - we'll package that into the security pack.

[08:10] Lena: Any gotchas you've seen with customers with complex transit gateway and multiple accounts?

[08:16] Ethan: Biggest issues are CIDR overlap and IAM scoping errors. Also cross-account PrivateLink requires careful principal permissions. We help with a pre-flight checklist and can run a short discovery agent to validate routes.

[08:29] Samir: What about model updates - if we need to push a new model, what's the patch flow?

[08:35] Maya: For Private you can either push models to an S3 bucket we both have access to via VPC endpoint, or Redwood can push into a private ECR/EFS. Updates can be scheduled with canary rollouts and automatic rollback on regressions.

[08:50] Lena: For compliance we may need penetration testing allowance and a shared responsibility matrix.

[08:57] Maya: Yes, we allow pen tests under a standard process and provide a shared responsibility doc. We'll include that.

[09:05] Speaker 2: (brief cross talk)

[09:08] Ethan: Quick note: If you have strict no-third-party-hosted-control-plane rules we can run a private control plane inside your VPC - we've done that with a few regulated customers. It increases setup time but meets strict compliance.

[09:24] Samir: That is probably our preference for production. Pilot can use Redwood-managed control plane if that's faster, but production should be VPC-only.

[09:33] Maya: Understood. We'll propose pilot with managed control plane and clearly documented migration path to VPC-hosted control plane.

[09:42] Hannah: Any limitations for HSM integration? We use an external HSM for key import.

[09:48] Ethan: We integrate with external HSMs for signing and key operations in the private deployment. We'll need a handshake of certificate exchange and network routes to the HSM endpoints. We'll document the process.

[09:59] Samir: Who will be our main Redwood contacts for the pilot?

[10:03] Maya: I'll be your AE. Ethan is the SE lead; we'll also loop in our Security PM, Carla, on the follow-up.

[10:12] Lena: Great. Let's recap next steps.

[10:15] Maya: Recap: 1) Ethan will schedule technical deep dive with Samir/Hannah (target 2026-06-23), 2) I will send SOC2 + security whitepaper + network req doc by 2026-06-20, 3) Samir will share VPC CIDRs, Transit Gateway topology, and any existing Peering constraints by 2026-06-22, 4) We'll propose pilot setup in us-east-1 with sample dedicated capacity and cost estimates.

[10:42] Lena: Sounds good. Any blockers we missed?

[10:45] Hannah: Nothing else from security for now. We'll review the pack and come back with questions.

[10:52] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the security pack.

[10:57] Meeting ended.

Notes: transcription contains minor speaker attribution errors and occasional filler words. References: security pack (link to be shared), network requirements doc (to be attached), pilot benchmark spreadsheet (TCO).
